Fix (abi.mojo _ensure_cpu_device, ABI 4.9): get-or-create the device in init and execute. Measured after the fix: rmsnorm/layernorm/sgemm return results from the main thread, from foreign threads, and when the first call is on a foreign thread; 64x512 rmsnorm with multiple workers ok; 40k foreign-thread calls RSS 27.7 -> 28.6 -> 28.6 MB (stable). rows.question: Is the Community licence's technical floor (one concurrent worker per device) enforced by the kernel libraries themselves, without a device login?
rows.claim: Yes. ABI §9: algenta_runtime_execute takes a device-wide slot via flock(LOCK_EX) on /dev/null inside the compiled library; blocking, crash-safe, fail-closed, no getenv. No scenario obtains more than one concurrent native worker.

Also the llm binary: flock import, both error codes, no getenv. Earlier dev-build runs (0.78-0.91) superseded.

rows.question: Can anyone on the internet — no Hugging Face token, empty cache — install a published kernel and run it, and is what they download capped to one worker per device?
rows.claim: Yes to both. As an anonymous user (HfApi(token=False), HF_TOKEN unset, fresh HF_HOME): get_kernel('thyn-ai/algenta-stats', version=1) downloads from the public Hub and returns correct statistics; the downloaded library imports flock, carries the §9 refusal code and has no getenv; the 9-scenario §9 gate holds ON THAT DOWNLOADED LIBRARY; every one of the 20 repositories has exactly one commit on v1 and main (the uncapped revisions are not retrievable).
rows.source: scripts/hf_kernels/verify_hub_capped.py --anon (this repository), 2026-09-22, macOS arm64; kernels 0.17.1, huggingface_hub 1.26.1
rows.result: Anonymous (no token, fresh HF_HOME), from the public Hub, run from scripts/hf_kernels/verify_hub_capped.py --anon: fit_normal(20k uniforms) mean=0.4998 std=0.2894 (expected 0.5 / 0.2887); downloaded library imports flock, carries the refusal code, no getenv; §9 gate ON THE DOWNLOADED LIBRARY, warm call 116 ms: (a) 0.81, (b) 0.82, (c) 0.85, (d) 0.86, (e) 0.79 effective workers (1.0 = one device-wide worker, bypass ≈ 4.0); SIGKILL holder -> next call 123 ms; queued while held 1.0 s -> 1137 ms clean; /dev/null unlink refused; (i) request_type_unsupported:ok request_not_json:ok request_not_json:ok invalid_arguments:ok function_not_registered:ok; history: 1 commit on v1 and main for all 20 repositories. ALL 9 SCENARIOS HELD.

rows.question: Is the GA wording — release stage, eligibility summary and support scope — drafted for owner approval (plan checkpoint L2)?
rows.claim: Drafted in PR #1131 as docs/hf-kernels/SUPPORT.md, mirroring established practice rather than invented text: GitLab's development-stage definitions (Generally Available / Preview / Not supported), the supported OS x arch x accelerator table from the capability manifest, Elastic's 'operating systems not listed are not supported' and six-month end-of-life window, what GA promises (additive v1 API enforced by the versioning gate, the compiled one-worker-per-device limit on every platform, manifest integrity checks) and does not (no load-time signature verification yet), the Community Use eligibility summary, and support channels. The kernel card gains a short Support section.
